validated_results.title: Modulation of the association between plasma intercellular adhesion molecule-1 and cancer risk by n-3 PUFA intake: a nested case-control study.
validated_results.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
validated_results.reason: The primary exposure is plasma sICAM-1 with n-3 PUFA intake serving only as a stratifying modifier, and the sole prostate-specific result is an interaction p value, so no separable PUFA-prostate cancer incidence estimate is reported.

validated_results.title: Predictors of 25-hydroxyvitamin D and its association with risk factors for prostate cancer: evidence from the prostate testing for cancer and treatment study.
validated_results.reason: The analysis develops a 25(OH)D prediction score among controls and relates it to prostate cancer risk factors (PSA, BMI, family history) without reporting any prostate cancer incidence result.

validated_results.reason: Prospective Finnish cohort reporting serum β-carotene concentration tertiles and risk of incident prostate cancer with an adjusted relative risk.

extraction.comparison_type: highest vs lowest tertile of serum β-carotene
extraction.population: 997 middle-aged Finnish men in the Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor (KIHD) cohort

sample_size.excerpt: The study population consisted of 997 middle-aged Finnish men (56.1 ± 6.6 yr) in the Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor (KIHD) cohort.

cases.excerpt: During the mean follow-up time of 15 yr, a total of 68 prostate cancer cases occurred.

effect_size.excerpt: After adjusting for age, examination yr, family history of cancer, BMI, pack-yr of smoking, alcohol consumption, education, physical activity, serum total cholesterol, and serum α-linolenic acid, men in the highest tertile of serum concentrations of β-carotene had 2.3-fold higher risk of prostate cancer as compared to those in the lowest tertile (RR = 2.29, 95% CI: 1.12-4.66; P = 0.023).

confidence_interval.excerpt: After adjusting for age, examination yr, family history of cancer, BMI, pack-yr of smoking, alcohol consumption, education, physical activity, serum total cholesterol, and serum α-linolenic acid, men in the highest tertile of serum concentrations of β-carotene had 2.3-fold higher risk of prostate cancer as compared to those in the lowest tertile (RR = 2.29, 95% CI: 1.12-4.66; P = 0.023).
